title: Mitigate ghost meter pulses from retry-fanout storms and add export-healing pass
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: Intermittent 'ghost' meter pulses (0.1-0.5 token pulses) were observed in hourly exports after a recent rate-limit retry policy change. These tiny pulses are creating noisy invoice lines and causing incorrect mid-cycle charge adjustments for a small subset of customers using bursty rate-limited endpoints. This ticket implements a two-part fix: (1) server-side suppression and dedup heuristics to prevent retry-fanout micro-pulses from being recorded as distinct usage events, and (2) an idempotent export-healing pass that consolidates sub-cent usage fragments prior to Stripe/NetSuite export.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No new hourly invoice anomalies traced to retry-driven micro-pulses for a 72-hour shadow-run on production traffic (validation dashboard shows <0.01% of accounts with fragmented pulses); 2) Export-healing pass runs as part of nightly export pipeline, consolidating pulses within the same tenant/timestamp-window and emitting deterministic export_line fingerprints; 3) All changes are covered by e2e tests and an integration test that replays previously recorded incident traces; 4) Rolloutable via feature flag with immediate rollback on any export checksum divergence.
implementation_notes: - Add a short-circuit in metering ingestion: discard pulses < 1 token if they occur within 3s of a prior pulse for the same (tenant, meter_key) and originate from retry path (request_metadata.retry=true). - Introduce sticky sampling of KV cache writes to avoid duplicate writes from concurrent retries (compare request_id and parent_attempt_id). - Export-healing transform: group meter events into 60s buckets per tenant/meter_key, merge events with total quantity < 1 token into a single line with canonical timestamp (start of bucket), and compute export_line_fingerprint = sha256(tenant|meter_key|bucket_start|qty). - Add gating flag billing.healing_v2 and a dry-run mode that annotates exports with heal_status:DRY_RUN/HEALED. - Add metrics: billing.ghost_pulse_count, billing.heal_merges, export.fingerprint_mismatch_count.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy ingestion suppression behind flag to 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor billing.ghost_pulse_count and cpu/latency; 2) Enable export-healing in dry-run for full tenant set for two nightly exports; compare checksums and run diff report to S3; 3) After 72h of stable diffs, flip healing to active for all exports; 4) Monitor post-rollout for two billing cycles and keep rollback playbook ready.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-eager suppression could drop legitimate sub-token meter events for valid micro-usage products. Mitigation: suppression has conservative threshold (1 token) and only applies to events marked retry=true. Export-healing is idempotent and runs as part of export pipeline with checksum gating to prevent accidental mutation of finalized exports. Manual reconciliation pathway (run-heal-repair job) available for flagged tenants.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for dedup logic and bucket merge behavior. - Integration test replaying SRE incident trace (see artifacts). - Shadow export run comparing legacy vs healed exports for three different tenant cohorts (low, med, high activity). - QA checklist: verify no loss of >1 token events, verify fingerprints stable across consecutive runs.
monitoring_and_alerts: - Alert if billing.ghost_pulse_count increases by >200% vs baseline. - Alert on export.fingerprint_mismatch_count > 0 after switching healing from DRY_RUN to ACTIVE. - Add dashboard panel 'Billing: Ghost Pulse & Healer' and link to runbook.
